Subject: sudden 5xx/timeouts across checkout — need immediate help

Karthik / Laura —

This is causing revenue impact — please treat as priority. We need an ETA for mitigation and customer-facing messaging.

— Sanjay

Karthik / David —

Short brief for execs (for the 10:30 leadership pulse):
1) Impact: FastBasket (high-velocity checkout partner, strategic merchant) experiencing ~5–6% checkout failures starting 08:45 PT; revenue at risk.
2) Cause hypothesis: elevated tail latency from dedicated pool serving rdx-bert-3 linked to sudden spike in sequence lengths + cache churn; runtime probes showing increased GPU kernel queueing.
3) Immediate mitigation: regional traffic re-route + temporary traffic split to quantized rdx-bert-3q; longer-term: capacity bump and eviction policy tune.

Decisions requested from leadership:
- Approve one-off credit for impacted window (recommend 40% pro-rata of API charges for 2 hours).
- Fast-track capacity increase on the dedicated pool for FastBasket (temp burst for 24 hours).

I'll be on the 10:30 leadership pulse to present.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: FastBasket — stabilization progress & next steps

Sanjay —

Summary of current state (15:40 PT):
- What we did: regional traffic split initiated at 10:05 PT; rollback of a small KV eviction change at 11:20 PT; promoted rdx-bert-3q to 22% of traffic starting 11:35 PT.
- Observable result: 5xx rate reduced from 6% -> 1.1% over the last 90 minutes; tail latency p95/p99 improved by ~55% / ~38% respectively. Client-side retries have dropped and checkout success is trending back to baseline.
- Quality: rdx-bert-3q shows minor reordering in non-critical suggestion slots; our QA sampling (50 sessions) shows no pricing-tag regressions. We will run a 200-session synthetic check before scaling fallback further.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) We recommend keeping rdx-bert-3q at 25% for the next 2 hours while we complete QA and then gradually reduce, unless you prefer a full cutover.
2) We propose a one-time 40% pro-rata credit for the impacted 2-hour window — Laura will circulate the proposed credit memo for approval.
3) Redwood infra will provision a 24-hour burst capacity to the dedicated pool; monitoring alerts tightened for sequence-length skew.

Customer-facing blurb (short): 
"We experienced elevated checkout failures earlier today affecting a subset of customers. Early mitigation steps have been applied and we expect normal service to continue. Our team is monitoring and will follow up with a full post-incident report."

If this aligns with you, we will post the note to your status page and proceed with the temporary capacity bump.

I'll keep the incident doc updated (link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aFastBasket-Incident-Notes) and send a final post-incident report within 48 hours.

— Karthik Iyer
